items.title: Europe wants champions again: is the age of the mega-merger returning?
items.excerpt: Key takeaways Europe is rethinking whether greater corporate scale can strengthen its competitiveness against larger United States and Asian rivals. Stock exchanges show the problem clearly: Europe has deep capital markets, but trading and infrastructure remain fragmented. Banks and telecoms face similar pressures , but bigger only creates value when scale improves the underlying economics. Europe has spent decades worrying about companies becoming too big. Now the bigger concern may be that they are not big enough. On 14 September 2026, Euronext chief executive St phane Boujnah said the pan-European exchange operator could be open to a combination with rival Deutsche B rse if the economics made sense. items.title: British Pound futures rebound as U.K. economic data beats expectations.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures tested their 200-day moving average before rebounding into positive territory, putting the contract on pace to snap a two-week streak of lower closes. The move was supported by stronger-than-expected U.K. economic data, with July GDP rising 0.4% and year-over-year growth hitting 1.6%. The robust data adds complexity to next Thursday's Bank of England meeting, where markets widely expect rates to remain at 3.75% amid pushback from Governor Andrew Bailey on the necessity of near-term hikes.

items.title: Treasury yields jump 24 bps as the Fed weighs a rate hike.
items.excerpt: Treasury yields are in focus for the week ahead after the 2-Year yield jumped 24 bps and the 5-Year yield rose 21 bps, marking the largest weekly increase since April 2025. The moves set the stage for a critical week of global central bank action. The FOMC announces its rate decision on Wednesday, accompanied by an updated Summary of Economic Projections. The probability of a 25 bps hike hit 86.5% following recent CPI data. Decisions from the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan follow on Thursday. The economic calendar also features U.S. Retail Sales, global CPI data, and regional manufacturing indicators, while the earnings slate remains light with five major companies reporting.

items.title: Euro FX futures hold range-bound as ECB hikes rates 25 bps.
items.excerpt: Todd Colvin unpacks the latest price action in Euro FX futures, which had a choppy session and settled near 1.1612 following the ECB's decision to hike rates by 25 basis points. With no clear guidance from President Lagarde on future moves, the market remains range-bound between 1.1550 and 1.1650. Colvin also highlights the CME Group Volatility Index (CVOL), noting that implied volatility remains firm across asset classes amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Looking ahead, focus shifts to the U.S. Consumer Price Index and its potential impact on next week's Federal Reserve meeting.

items.title: Crude oil tops $100 amid Middle East tensions.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners recaps the morning's market action, noting early declines across U.S. equities with Nasdaq-100 futures leading the drop. He examines the surge in crude oil past the $100 mark as Middle East geopolitical risks escalate. Iaccino also covers the European Central Bank's decision to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points and its impact on the euro. Finally, he previews the economic calendar, highlighting a $22 billion 30-Year Treasury bond auction, the ongoing corporate earnings slate, and upcoming gross domestic product and inflation data.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures rally ahead of Bank of Japan rate decision.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures saw upward momentum, rallying in four of the last five sessions to climb 4.45% above the September low. The price action comes as the market anticipates a potential 25 bps rate increase at the upcoming Sept. 18 Bank of Japan meeting. Ongoing policy coordination between Tokyo and the U.S. Treasury, underscored by the July 31 yen intervention funded via euro reserves, continues to influence the currency's trajectory. Despite a softer second-quarter GDP revision, broader market expectations suggest economic conditions pose no immediate obstacle to further rate adjustments.

He breaks down the Treasury's expanded buyback program for older 10-Year and 30-Year securities, designed to improve liquidity and ease pressure on longer-term yields. Bob also previews the upcoming ECB rate decision, where markets anticipate a 25 bps rate hike following a recent jump in inflation, and outlines the heavy slate of earnings, auctions, and economic data ahead.

Markets are currently pricing in a 25 basis point rate hike from the ECB, but attention remains focused on guidance regarding future policy if inflation remains elevated. Colvin highlights that despite upcoming risk events—including the ECB decision and U.S. CPI data—the CVOL index shows volatility dropping to three-week lows.
